2017-05-09 · dismissal. On Tuesday 9 May 2017 President Adama Barrow dismissed the governor of the Central Bank of The Gambia, Amadou Colley, together with his deputies Basiru Njai and Oumie Savage-Samba and the bank's director of finance, Ousainou Corr. No reason was given. Colley told Reuters that they received their letters that day without being given any reason for the sacking, the letters stating only that their services had been terminated with immediate effect. He had been governor since 2010, appointed under Yahya Jammeh, who lost the December 2016 election and left the country in January 2017 after weeks of diplomatic pressure. Barrow, who inherited a state whose institutions were still largely staffed by Jammeh's allies, had been progressively replacing officials in key positions to establish his authority. The bank's own research economist, Bakary Jammeh, was named governor. The dismissals came while inflation was high and the dalasi was depreciating. Colley said he was surprised at his unceremonious removal and was proud to have served the country for more than three decades. This is separate from what the Janneh Commission later found about his conduct as governor under Jammeh, which is recorded as a corruption case: the commission was only established in June 2017, a month after he was removed, so the dismissal was not a consequence of its findings. The Gambia: Jammeh-era central bank chief fired without reasons (Africanews, citing Reuters)

current_paragraph: The Reserve Bank of Malawi issues the kwacha, and presidents have removed its leaders twice. President Joyce Banda removed governor Perks Ligoya, according to two unnamed sources, with Charles Chuka reportedly chosen to succeed him and no official reason given; the date is not stated. Newly elected president Lazarus Chakwera dismissed governor Dalitso Kabambe and appointed Wilson Banda on 8 July 2020. After a forensic audit of the bank's payments between January 2019 and June 2020, the state charged Kabambe and three others with abuse of office, negligence, money laundering and causing loss of public funds, alleging that 4.3 billion kwacha went to FDH Bank without board approval; pleas were not taken because the charges were subject to change, and nothing is proven. In December 2021 police arrested Kabambe and Joseph Mwanamvekha, saying the two procured and masterminded the falsification of gross liability and net reserve base returns to make the International Monetary Fund believe Malawi was meeting the conditions of its Extended Credit Facility loan; that too stands only as an accusation. In January 2026 President Peter Mutharika appointed Henry Mathanga deputy governor, although the bank had dismissed him after a disciplinary inquiry and he faces criminal charges, and critics say the appointment breaches section 16(2) of the Reserve Bank of Malawi Act. Its 2,000-kwacha note is printed by Giesecke & Devrient. Malawi scores 37 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence. President Lazarus Chakwera dismissed the governor he had himself installed: having removed Dalitso Kabambe in July 2020 and appointed Wilson Banda, he dismissed Banda in early January 2025 and moved up the deputy governor, MacDonald Mafuta Mwale. One career move is documented, and it is Mafuta Mwale's: he served as Secretary to the Treasury, the senior civil service post in the finance ministry, with no years given for it, was redeployed back to the Reserve Bank in January of the previous year, two years after that post, and was its deputy governor until he was appointed Governor with immediate effect, as reported on 7 January 2025, subject to confirmation by Parliament's Public Appointments Committee. The government's statement thanked Banda and gave no reason; Nyasa Times reported that the President had been demanding monetary reforms since June of the previous year and that a source close to State House said the results were painfully slow. Banda had devalued the kwacha by about 25 percent in May 2022, calling it a necessary evil to align the supply of foreign exchange with the fundamentals, and by a further 44 percent in November 2023, and the gap with the parallel market widened after both. Malawian civil society organisations said in January 2026 that the dismissal of the whole board at the time breached the Reserve Bank of Malawi Act's requirement of continuity in leadership, and that one of those removed was targeted for perceived political associations; Nyasa Times reported instead that he had been removed after a formal disciplinary inquiry under the Act and faced criminal charges. The two accounts have not been reconciled.

Malawi: Outrage As Mutharika Appoints Fired and Charged Mathanga As RBM Deputy Governor (Nyasa Times via allAfrica, 11 Jan 2026)
2025-01 · dismissal. President Lazarus Chakwera dismissed the governor of the Reserve Bank of Malawi, Wilson Banda, in early January 2025, and appointed the deputy governor, MacDonald Mafuta Mwale, in his place; the government's statement thanked Banda for his service and gave no reason. Nyasa Times reported that the decision stemmed from the President's frustration that Banda had not implemented the monetary reforms the President had been demanding since June of the previous year, quoting a source close to State House saying Banda had been given the mandate to fix monetary policy but that the results were painfully slow and far from the transformative changes the President envisioned. Banda had devalued the kwacha by 25 to 27 percent in May 2022, calling it a necessary evil to align the supply of foreign exchange with the fundamentals, and by a further 44 percent in November 2023; the gap with the parallel market widened after both. A second, disputed episode runs alongside this one. Malawian civil society organisations, the Black Economic Empowerment Movement and the Forum for National Development, said in January 2026 that the dismissal of the whole Reserve Bank board at the time, including senior executives, violated the Reserve Bank of Malawi Act's requirement of continuity in leadership, that they had warned the government the mass dismissal was illegal and exposed the bank to manipulation, and that one of those removed, Henry Mathanga, was targeted for perceived political associations rather than misconduct. Against that, Nyasa Times reported that Mathanga had been removed after a formal disciplinary inquiry under the Act and was facing criminal charges in the Financial Crimes Division of the High Court. The two accounts of why he was removed have not been reconciled in the sources read. His later reappointment is recorded separately, as an appointment. current_paragraph: South Sudan's money is the South Sudanese pound, issued by the Bank of South Sudan, and its notes are printed by De La Rue, which won a contract for 2.8 billion banknotes in 2011. The country scores 39 of 100 for exposure to outside influence, where 100 means fully exposed, almost all of it from corruption in the country. current_paragraph: El Salvador's central bank is the Central Reserve Bank of El Salvador, and the currency is listed as both the colon and the US dollar. The IMF's 2023 classification puts the country among places with no separate legal tender of their own, using the US dollar as their anchor; legal changes made private acceptance of Bitcoin voluntary and tax payments payable only in US dollars, listed as steps taken before an IMF loan approved on 26 February 2025. One episode with parliament is recorded. In September 2020 Nicolas Martinez, president of the bank, answered a summons from a Legislative Assembly commission investigating the debt the government had taken on during the COVID-19 pandemic and how it was used, and resigned the day after appearing; no reason for the resignation is given. Deputies asked whether the release of banks' liquidity reserve was designed so banks could buy Treasury paper, and he answered that it was an autonomous decision of the banks. One career move is recorded, and it stays within the public sector: Carlos Paredes came to the presidency of the bank from the Autonomous Port Executive Commission, the National Centre for Agricultural and Forestry Technology, the National Council for Science and Technology and the Ministry of Economy. On its reserves, the bank's own document on international reserves management says it joined the World Bank's Reserve Advisory and Management Partnership in 2010, which it describes as advice on reserve management rather than managing a portfolio, and it names no external portfolio manager or custodian, referring only generally to external investment portfolio managers. The Corte de Cuentas de la Republica audits the accounts under a law still in force. El Salvador scores 39 of 100, where 100 means fully exposed to outside influence.

current_paragraph: Bhutan's central bank is the Royal Monetary Authority, which issues the ngultrum and keeps it pegged, or fixed, to the Indian rupee; the rupee circulates in the country as well. The head of state names its board. On 4 May 2026 President Mahmoud Abbas issued a decree reconstituting the board of directors, acting on a recommendation from the Cabinet and from the Authority's Governor. Three of the eight seats are held by virtue of law: the Governor as chairman, the Deputy Governor, and a representative of the Ministry of Finance, named as Majdi Al-Hassan. The law that created the bank in 1997, with one reform since 1970, gives it a legal independence score of 0.435 of 1, ranking 155 of 191.
